events.factual_description: The Hamilton Live lists Chopteeth Afrofunk Big Band with Corey Arceneaux & Zydeco Hot Peppers for Saturday, October 31, 2026 at 8:00 PM in Washington, DC under the subtitle Halloween Monster Mosh. The venue calendar lists tickets at $25-$50 and links to an authorized See Tickets/EVENTIM destination. Chopteeth's official biography describes the Washington-based group as an 11-piece Afrofunk orchestra built around Afrobeat, modern jazz, Yoruba-derived rhythm, funk, highlife and other African dance-music traditions. Corey Arceneaux's official site identifies him as founder, accordionist, organist and vocalist of the Zydeco Hot Peppers and documents a multigenerational Creole accordion lineage extending back to his great-grandfather. His 2026 album Accordion Man marks forty years as an accordionist. The Hamilton does not publish event-specific individual personnel beyond the billed acts, so no additional musicians are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This is a local groove collision with an actual musical reason to exist. Chopteeth brings an 11-piece Washington Afrofunk engine built from horns, percussion and the long-cycle logic of Afrobeat; Corey Arceneaux brings accordion-led Creole zydeco whose dance pulse comes from a completely different lineage. Putting those vocabularies on the same Hamilton bill makes the night about how two rhythm-first traditions move a room, not about an arbitrary Halloween package.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for this if October 31 is open in the DMV and groove-driven cross-cultural music is part of the thread. The Hamilton is a good scale for both the mass of Chopteeth's horns and percussion and the bite of zydeco accordion, but both acts remain active performers, so I would still keep a genuinely singular farewell, premiere or once-only lineup ahead of it if the calendar collides.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí sí hay una colisión local de grooves con una razón musical real. Chopteeth trae una máquina afrofunk de once músicos construida en Washington alrededor de metales, percusión y la lógica de ciclo largo del afrobeat; Corey Arceneaux llega desde otra genealogía completamente distinta, con acordeón, tradición criolla y el pulso de baile del zydeco. Poner esos dos lenguajes en la misma noche de The Hamilton vuelve el cartel una conversación sobre cómo dos tradiciones centradas en el ritmo mueven un salón, no un paquete arbitrario de Halloween.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente si el 31 de octubre está libre en el DMV y el hilo de groove y cruces culturales está presente. The Hamilton tiene buena escala tanto para la masa de metales y percusión de Chopteeth como para el filo del acordeón zydeco; aun así, ambas bandas siguen activas, así que mantendría por delante una despedida realmente singular, un estreno o una alineación de una sola oportunidad si hubiera choque de fechas.
